clue.text: Picture harbour, one with sailor round about

parts.note: a port is a harbour town or haven

indicators.note: about signals that the sailor-and-one unit is turned to read backwards
round tells us the sailor's letters wrap around the numeral one

parts.note: TAR is a familiar old word for a sailor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to depict a harbour scene with a sailor somewhere in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators act in turn: 'round' wraps the sailor about the one, then 'about' turns that whole unit backwards before it joins the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted likeness of a person is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Power in writing about the Northern view

indicators.note: in puts the power letter inside the writing

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
P is the symbol for power in physics
C stands for circa, Latin for about
in northern English dialect the is shortened to t'

explanation.surface: An essay on electricity supply in the North of England.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech 'the' is clipped to t', so 'the Northern' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide outlook or scene.

clue.text: Anger about pre-Christian date ascribed to some bones

indicators.note: about means the anger wraps around the date

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
1 BC, a year before the Christian era, written I BC

explanation.surface: Fury over carbon-dating that puts some bones before Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: The date is the year 1 BC, written with the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribs together form the ribcage, a set of bones.

clue.text: Bright, not black and wet

indicators.note: not removes the black letter from the clever word

parts.note: a bright pupil is clever, brainy
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Weather that is sunny, then no longer dark but drizzly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainy weather is wet weather.

clue.text: Cheerful transplant patient's hopes lie here?

explanation.surface: A heart recipient stays upbeat about the new organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in good spirits, and literally a recipient of a new organ hopes it is a sound, healthy one.

clue.text: River calms around first sign of Henley

indicators.note: around says the taming verb wraps the letter taken from Henley

parts.note: to calm an animal is to tame it, so calms gives tames

indicators.note: first sign of picks only the opening letter of the town's name

explanation.surface: Picture the river settling down as the regatta town of Henley approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames hosts a famous rowing regatta, so the town sits naturally in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through London and past Henley.

clue.text: Rugby player appearing in 2 pantomime?

explanation.surface: A rugby star making a festive stage appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins is a London rugby union club; Harlequin is also the masked clown of the old harlequinade. The '2' in the clue as held is most likely 'a' misread.
explanation.definitionFit: A player for the Harlequins club; also the stock clown character of English pantomime.

clue.text: With a switch, most of monolith is illuminated at night

indicators.note: a switch is a swap, so the letters change places
most of drops the last letter of the standing stone

explanation.surface: A great stone is lit up at night once someone flicks a switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the H, and 'With a switch' rearranges MONOLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit by the moon describes something lit up after dark.

clue.text: Perceptive, a little, about women

indicators.note: about means the scrap goes around the women's letter

parts.note: a shred is a tiny scrap, a little

explanation.surface: Showing some insight into women.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and sharp-witted, quick to see things.

clue.text: Neat game from universities

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A tidy game played between two old colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like an adjective meaning tidy; it is the old noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The blend name for Oxford and Cambridge, the two oldest English universities taken together.

clue.text: It protects King in love-affair

indicators.note: in places the king's letter inside the love affair

parts.note: amour is a borrowed word for a love affair
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch shielded inside a romantic entanglement.
explanation.definitionFit: Plate or mail worn in battle is protective covering.

clue.text: Sick of mountains?

explanation.surface: Feeling ill at the thought of high places.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaky means pale and unwell in British use; read as peak plus -y it means full of mountain summits.

clue.text: Secret society member left over some associate

parts.note: an odd sock is one left over from a pair
a fellow is a companion or associate

explanation.surface: A member of a secret society who is the spare one among the group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society with lodges and rituals, hence 'secret society'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of one of the fraternal orders with lodges and initiation rites.

clue.text: Sticking to principles is unusual in a director

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of the phrase are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: An observation that principled film directors are rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidly applying theory regardless of practical concerns.

clue.text: Find royal circle not guilty -in camera, presumably

explanation.surface: A judge acquits the whole royal entourage behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in parts it is acquit (clear) the royal household (the court); as a phrase it means to empty a courtroom so the hearing is held privately.

clue.text: No car seen in pieces from this vibration

indicators.note: in pieces means the words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: After a crash, no car is visible, only a shuddering vibration.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is sympathetic vibration that reinforces a sound.

clue.text: Congenial scripture lessons finish in rush

indicators.note: in places the lessons and the finish inside the rushing word

parts.note: to fly is to rush along
RI, religious instruction, is the old school name for scripture lessons
end means finish

explanation.surface: Bible classes that end in a hurry are pleasant enough.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (religious instruction) was the British school subject teaching scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and agreeable company is congenial company.

clue.text: Provider of Meals on Wheels?

parts.note: the charity service delivering food to the housebound is reread as a railway dining carriage serving food on wheels

explanation.surface: A question about who runs the charity delivering hot food to elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: Meals on Wheels is a British charity delivering hot meals to elderly people at home; here the wheels are a train's.
explanation.definitionFit: A train carriage where passengers are served meals while travelling.

clue.text: Appearance of prototype part not allowed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: a part is a role, and out means not allowed

explanation.surface: A component left out of the first model of a new product.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLE (part) and OUT (not allowed) sound like ROLL-OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The launch or first public showing of a new aircraft or product.

clue.text: Composer to get a load of real estate

parts.note: cop a load of is slang for get a load of, so cop means get
land is real estate

explanation.surface: A musician buying up a large amount of property.
explanation.walkthrough: Aaron Copland was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The American composer of Appalachian Spring.

clue.text: Pointed remark about one cold medicine having effect on the digestion

definitions.text: medicine having effect on the digestion

indicators.note: about puts the remark around the number and the temperature letter

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark
I is the Roman numeral for one
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A dig about someone taking a medicine for a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda is taken as an antacid for indigestion.

clue.text: I throw away a lot in part of London

parts.note: to sling something is to throw it away
tons means a great deal, a lot

explanation.surface: Someone discarding plenty of rubbish somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLINGTON is a borough of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A north London borough, one district of the capital.

clue.text: Plan on receiving the French national symbol

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A scheme for adopting the French emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The maple leaf is Canada's emblem, appearing on its flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree whose leaf is the Canadian emblem.

clue.text: Inspiration running short, see, in symphony, perhaps

annotationWithheld.why: Inspiration running short, see, in symphony, perhaps: MUS(E) + C gives MUSC; no word supplies the I (likely 'I see' with the I lost in OCR), no scan to confirm
annotationWithheld.clue: Inspiration running short, see, in symphony, perhaps

clue.text: Relative accepts second sum

indicators.note: accepts means the relative takes in the brief moment

parts.note: an aunt is a family relative
mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: A family member agrees to a second sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A total or quantity is a sum.

clue.text: Tree not readily moved for treatment

parts.note: the fir is a conifer
staid means sedate and settled, not easily stirred

explanation.surface: A firmly rooted tree resists being dug up and shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' suggests an anagram, but 'not readily moved' is a definition of STAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency help given to the injured is immediate treatment.

clue.text: First slice of bread complete — with this?

definitions.text: First slice of bread complete — with this?

indicators.note: first slice of takes just the opening letter of bread

parts.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: Cutting a first slice, ready to make it whole with a spread.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a slice of bread is complete once spread with this.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy spread for a slice of bread.

clue.text: Day cadet needs to get drunk -leaves for drink here?

indicators.note: getting drunk scrambles the letters of day cadet

explanation.surface: A non-boarding cadet must get drunk on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' are tea leaves, not time off; a day cadet is one who lives at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The small box where tea leaves are stored before brewing.
